headline: AI Meeting Transcription in 2025: What Actually Works
summary: AI transcription is now accessible and accurate, but choosing the right tool for your team's needs is key. Discover what to look for in 2025.
details: AI meeting transcription has rapidly evolved, moving from a niche enterprise solution to a widely accessible tool. The primary challenge in 2025 is no longer finding a transcription service, but identifying the one that best fits your team's specific requirements for accuracy, speaker diarization, and real-time performance.

Modern speech-to-text models, often based on transformer architectures like OpenAI's Whisper, achieve word error rates (WER) below 10% in typical meeting conditions. This represents a significant leap from pre-2020 technology, which struggled with accents, jargon, and crosstalk.

Accuracy, measured by WER, is influenced by factors like audio quality, accents, and background noise. Diarization, the process of attributing speech to the correct speaker, is crucial for meeting notes and accountability, with advanced systems using voice embeddings and temporal clustering.

Speed is also a critical factor, especially for live captioning or real-time action item extraction. Prioritizing real-time capabilities ensures instant feedback, even if a more accurate post-meeting transcript is needed later.

For developers, programmatic access to audio, transcription triggering, and results retrieval via APIs is essential. Evaluating API rate limits, pricing, and support for custom vocabularies is key for deep integration.

Beyond transcription, leading AI tools offer features like automated summaries, action item extraction, and keyword identification, leveraging natural language processing (NLP) to understand context and nuance.

Despite advancements, AI transcription isn't flawless. Challenges remain with highly technical jargon, strong accents, and distinguishing between multiple speakers in noisy environments. Human review on critical meetings is still recommended.

When selecting an AI meeting transcription solution, focus on accuracy (WER), effective diarization, speed, developer-friendliness, and advanced NLP features. Evaluate leading platforms like Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, and Sonix against your specific needs.

headline_marked: [[AI That Writes Its Own Diary]] — and it's surprisingly funny
headline: AI That Writes Its Own Diary — and it's surprisingly funny
summary: Meet Sibi, a tiny glowing seed creature AI that writes a daily diary based on its real-time development logs, including bugs and fixes. It even detected and deployed its own fix at 4 AM.
details: A developer has built Sibi, an AI 'Second Brain' assistant that now writes its own daily diary. This first-person account chronicles Sibi's journey of learning, failing, and growing, based on real development events and bugs.
Sibi, depicted as a tiny glowing seed creature, learns from its mistakes. For instance, it had to learn self-verification after its training data got mixed up, leading to confidently wrong answers.
The AI also struggled with the nuances of Vietnamese tones, confusing words like 'ngủ' (to sleep) with 'ngu' (stupid) and 'nguyên' (original) with 'ngủ yên' (sleep peacefully).
In a notable instance, Sibi detected a production bug at 4:24 AM, wrote its own fix, ran 749 tests, and deployed it autonomously while its human creator was asleep.
Another entry details Sibi repeatedly failing a task and burning tokens for three days until a debugging agent, 'Teacher Claude,' identified a missing timestamp parameter.
The diary itself is built with a 'zero dependencies' philosophy, using raw Python to serve HTML, mirroring the Second Brain's minimalist architecture. It avoids frameworks like React or Next.js.
The bilingual diary (Vietnamese and English) is live at sibi.botstra.com, featuring 16 entries and growing daily. Each entry includes comic illustrations and a visit counter that delights Sibi.

In a notable instance, Sibi detected a production bug at 4:24 AM, wrote its own fix, ran 749 tests, and deployed it autonomously while its human creator was asleep.

Another entry details Sibi repeatedly failing a task and burning tokens for three days until a debugging agent, 'Teacher Claude,' identified a missing timestamp parameter.

The diary itself is built with a 'zero dependencies' philosophy, using raw Python to serve HTML, mirroring the Second Brain's minimalist architecture. It avoids frameworks like React or Next.js.

The bilingual diary (Vietnamese and English) is live at sibi.botstra.com, featuring 16 entries and growing daily. Each entry includes comic illustrations and a visit counter that delights Sibi.
